Nagoji matches 9.2 in costume (dhoti, binding, shoulder cloth), with a clean chin (faint shading only), a flush gold stud and no grey. Same cellar, tall lamp and door as 9.1 and 9.2. Hands are sound. The large plain wall between and above them gives room for both of Revathi's balloons.

Clean. Revathi matches her sheet: indigo sari with the pallu over her shoulder, jasmine braid, flat-coin necklace, gold armlets, sandalwood line, and no tali or red dot. She wears a small private smile and glances to the right, toward where Nagoji lay in 9.3. The same cellar door and timber ceiling show. The lamp is a tall standing brass lamp rather than the small one in 9.1. That is a minor difference and is acceptable in a close-up background. The upper right wall between her head and the door is clear for both balloons. Nagoji is off-panel to the right.

Shows the beat: Nagoji alone, sitting up on the mat and looking at the low door, with dawn in thin blades through its cracks. The brass lamp is out with one thread of smoke rising, and the other half of the mat is empty. Minor drift: a few faint grey strands at the temple (no grey is wanted on page 9). His shoulder cloth has a gold border, where 9.1 has a plain one. The rib binding is hidden under the draped cloth. The brand sits high near the elbow on the visible face of the forearm, small at panel scale. The large plain wall in the upper middle holds both captions.

Clean. A close strip of Nagoji's bare forearm and hand resting palm-down on the empty mat, with dhoti at left, beside a cold low brass bowl lamp with a burnt-out wick. Thin dawn light comes through the cracks of the low door. The lamp matches the burned-out bowl lamp in 9.5. The hand is sound: four fingers visible, thumb tucked. No face is shown, and the upper mud wall gives a wide low-detail band for the long caption. v01 is not a listed candidate; its lamp is still lit and the sleeve is wrong.

v01 sets the scene well: wet mossy river steps, clear river, rows of brass ghee lamps, a Kerala temple wall, and Nagoji barefoot in rust-red turban, cream tunic and red sash with a clean chin, gold stud and no grey. The problem is Varma, the bare-chested man in white at the head of the party. He has a prominent grey streak at the temple, loose shoulder-length curls and a gold ear stud, so he reads as Nagoji's later-life sheet rather than the V13 Varma face. That breaks the grey-as-clock rule the page header sets up, because readers will take the grey as Nagoji's. It also clashes with the black-haired Varma in 10.2 to 10.5.
decisions.correction: Draw Marthanda Varma, the bare-chested man in the plain white cloth at the head of the party, from the V13 varma-v1 sheet, and make sure he does not resemble Nagoji. Give him jet-black hair with NO grey or silver streak anywhere, gathered in a knot above his LEFT ear, not loose shoulder-length curls. Use the V13 Varma face (a longer, narrower jaw, curled moustache, red-and-white Vaishnavite forehead mark). He wears no earrings, no gold ear stud and no jewellery, and a narrow linen dressing on his left shoulder sits half hidden under the white cloth. Keep everything else as it is: the wet, mossy black stone steps running into the clear river, the rows of brass ghee lamps along the temple wall, the white royal parasol and the barefoot attendants behind, and Nagoji walking barefoot at Varma's side in rust-red turban, cream tunic with pushed-up sleeves and broad red sash, with a thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, small gold ear stud and no grey at the temples. Leave the open sky at upper right clear for two captions.

decisions.issues: Minor only. The left-shoulder dressing is not visible because it is the far shoulder under the cloth, which reads as 'half hidden'. There is a faint touch of grey at Varma's sideburn. The tall brass lamp stands read slightly like candles. The beat is clear: barefoot, no crown or jewels, plain white cloth, gold and pepper sacks laid before the dark inner shrine. The dark upper-left hall gives clean caption space.

v01 has the right beat and a good priest: the V13 temple priest carries the sword across both palms toward Varma's open hands, in a dark granite corridor with a lit sanctum. But Varma wears two long strands of gold bead necklaces. The script says no jewels for this visit, and both neighbouring panels (10.2 kneeling, 10.4 riding) show him without any, so the costume jumps mid-scene. His face also reads younger than the V13 Varma in 10.2. The sword has a diamond-wrapped black grip and a ring/disc guard that reads as a Japanese or European hybrid, not a Kerala royal blade, and it does not match the plain gilt hilt in 10.4.
decisions.correction: Marthanda Varma wears NO jewellery in this panel: no gold bead necklaces, no chains, no earrings. He wears only the plain white cloth over his left shoulder, with a narrow linen dressing half hidden beneath it, exactly as in the neighbouring panels where he kneels at the shrine and rides home. Draw his face from the V13 varma-v1 sheet as a mature man in his thirties, not a youth, with black hair in a knot and the Vaishnavite forehead mark. The sword is a long, straight Kerala royal blade with a plain gilt brass hilt: round pommel, short straight crossguard and a plain dark grip, with no braided or diamond-wrapped grip and no ring or disc guard. Keep everything else: the priest from the V13 temple-priest sheet carrying the sword flat across both open palms and laying it into Varma's cupped hands, the dark granite corridor with the lamp-lit inner sanctum behind, the brass oil lamps with open wicks, and a dark, low-detail band at the top of the frame for the caption.

decisions.issues: Minor only. Varma's hair is loose curls with a small topknot rather than the knot of 10.2, and he has a leather riding shoe in the stirrup. Kayal's black lower legs are out of frame, but her bay coat and black mane match. Nagoji is on the sheet (rust-red turban, cream tunic, red sash, thick curled moustache, clean chin, gold stud, no grey) and is watching Varma. Varma has no crest and no jewels and holds the sheathed straight sword across his lap with both hands. The green paddy country is right, and the upper-centre and upper-right sky hold both captions clear of faces.

It hits the scripted beat: a 3:1 strip where the bare straight sword across Varma's white-clad knees is the subject, with a sun flare on its edge, and the small column of riders behind on the red track through wet paddy and palms. Varma's dark, black-maned horse matches 10.4, his face is out of frame, the hands are sound, there is no text, and clear blue sky at upper right takes the caption. Minor points. The lead escort rider, in a rust turban and cream tunic, has a short black beard and rides a bay with a white blaze and white socks, so a close reader could take him as a bearded Nagoji on the wrong horse. He is tiny (face about 40 px high), and a second rider also wears a saffron turban, so he reads as escort. A touch-up (white turban or clean chin) is worth considering. The sword's guard is a small lozenge rather than the plain straight bar of 10.3. Small white pennons on two spears are not war banners.

Minor: Lannoy stands just behind Ramayyan at the table rather than clearly apart beside it, and has a faint white rim outline. Both principals match their sheets (Lannoy in white tunic-coat over white mundu, not blue). Caption space: open sky top centre-right (x 0.62-0.88, y 0-0.15) and wall above the awning top-left.

Framing departs from the script: Nagoji is a large over-the-shoulder foreground figure on the left rather than a small figure on a bastion lip, and he looks across more than down. The high angle over angled, sloped star-trace bastions (under construction, matching the half-built parapet in 11.4) still carries the beat. Nagoji matches: rust-red turban, red sash, thick moustache, clean chin, gold ear stud, no grey. Caption space: the sky band along the top (x 0.22-1.0, y 0-0.08) and the low-detail parapet stones bottom-left (x 0-0.45, y 0.86-1.0). The 11.3 inset can sit top-right over the distant landscape.
Clean. Tall square-cornered Deccan fort on a crag in dry ochre colours. The unlettered saffron swallow-tailed pennant suits a memory panel. Wide open sky top-left for the caption.

Clean. Lannoy matches his sheet (white tunic-coat, white mundu, sandals, pale hair with a black ribbon) and is kneeling, tracing angled lines in wet clay with a stick. The squat, heavy mason ponders the sketch. The clay drawing has no letters. Open sky top centre-right (x 0.42-0.98, y 0-0.13) holds both Lannoy balloons.

Minor only. The clay sketch on the slab is a plain grid rather than the star trace drawn in 11.4. Lannoy is brushing dust off his thighs and mundu rather than his knees exactly. Otherwise it is clean. Lannoy matches his sheet: pale curly hair with a black ribbon, white tunic-coat, mundu and sandals, no blue coat. The mason is the same one as in 11.4 (beard, headband, striped shoulder cloth) and rests his hand on the old wall with an unconvinced look. The setting is the same parapet. There is no painted text, and hands and anatomy are sound. Open sky fills the upper frame above both men for the MASON and LANNOY balloons.

Clean. Lannoy matches his sheet: pale wavy hair with a black ribbon, white stand-collar tunic-coat over a white mundu, sandals. He stands before a line of bare-chested Nair musketeers in dhotis drilling with upright muskets, with a cannon crew beyond. Hands are sound and there is no text. The plain white flag carries no emblem. Open sky across the top centre and right gives room for both Lannoy lines.

Nagoji wears a buttoned blue Travancore drill coat over his tunic. The script and bible allow the blue coat only on parade day (14.2), and 12.2 is an ordinary afternoon drill. A grey streak shows at his temple, but the script's grey schedule has none from 10.1 to 14.3 and 12.2 says 'no grey yet'. With both sleeves rolled, a long white scar shows on the RIGHT (sword-arm) forearm as well as the left, but brand and scar belong only on the inner LEFT forearm. Megha (dappled grey, black mane and tail), the riders wheeling on sand, and the sky are good.
decisions.correction: Nagoji wears NO blue coat in this panel. The blue Travancore drill coat is for parade day only (14.2), and this is an ordinary afternoon drill. Dress him exactly on the commander sheet: rust-red turban, cream tunic with both sleeves down to the wrists, broad red sash over the shoulder and round the waist, cream trousers, boots, talwar in his right hand. His long curly hair is entirely black with NO grey or silver at the temples. Give him a thick curled moustache, a clean-shaven chin and a small gold ear stud. Neither forearm shows any scar, brand or mark. Keep Megha exactly as drawn: a dappled grey with a black mane and tail, in full stride on the sand. Keep the afternoon drill ground with the fort wall, palms, open sky and the troop of Travancore horse wheeling in a loose circle around him with raised talwars. Dress those riders like the distant horsemen of 12.4, in plain cream tunics with red waist sashes, so that no one on the page wears a blue coat before the parade. No text, letters or emblems on any flag.

decisions.issues: Acceptable with minor notes. Nagoji is on the sheet: rust-red turban, thick curled moustache, clean chin, gold ear stud, no grey, red sash, boots, talwar. Lannoy is in the white coat and mundu, looking down and tracing rectangles in the dust with his toe. He wears sandals (the bible's 16-23 row) rather than the script's 'boot'. A tiny pale twig shows at his toe. With the arms crossed, the brand reads on the left forearm, but nearer the elbow than a hand's width above the wrist, and the long white scar is not shown. The background musketeers wear white tunics, trousers, boots and turbans, unlike 12.1's bare-chested Nairs in dhotis. Lannoy speaks first but stands to the right of Nagoji, so the letterer should stack Lannoy's balloon higher in the open sky at upper right and Nagoji's below it.

Acceptable with minor notes. Lannoy is breaking into a laugh, hand on hip, in the white coat and mundu with pale hair and a black ribbon. Nagoji stands beside him with arms crossed and a wry look, matching the face lock: thick curled moustache, clean chin, gold ear stud, no grey. A knot of soldiers behind watches, some amused. Hands are sound and there is no text. The brand and scar sit on the top (left) forearm, but nearer the elbow than a hand's width above the wrist. A small wooden frame of two posts and a crossbeam on the wall at right loosely recalls a gallows, but it has no rope or noose. The background soldiers wear cream tunics, blue turbans, cross-belts and boots, unlike 12.1's bare-chested Nairs. Open sky across the top centre and right holds the three balloons.

Clean. Varma in V13 court dress with crest, necklaces and spear, pointing over the pass. Ramayyan with palm-leaf bundle and stylus. Lannoy in white tunic-coat, mundu and sandals. Nagoji: rust-red turban, red sash, curled moustache, clean chin, gold stud. Hands are sound and there is no text. Open sky at top right holds both Varma lines. Note: Nagoji shows no grey here, but the ch16 bible row asks for first grey at the temples (the script says 'no grey yet'), and panels 2 and 5 show grey. The author needs to settle which is right; I did not resolve it.

Acceptable. Minor points: (1) Framing is a medium two-shot, not a true close on Varma with Nagoji at the frame edge, but Varma's sideways look at Nagoji reads clearly. (2) Nagoji has first grey at the temple, which follows the ch16 bible row but not the script's 'no grey yet', and panels 1 and 4 show none. (3) The brand and the thin white scar are correctly on the pushed-up LEFT forearm, but the brand sits mid-forearm (the wrist is off-frame). No text. Hands are sound. Sky at top centre holds the line.

Varma matches neither his sheet nor the bible's field look. He has grey-streaked temples, a topknot on the crown instead of the side knot above his LEFT ear, and a small gold ear stud instead of pearl drops, with no forehead mark. He reads like Nagoji's later-life topknot look. He also looks at the officers, not toward the distant sea and the Dutch ships the script calls for. And Nagoji's long white scar is drawn on his RIGHT forearm (the brand is on the left), which contradicts the ch16 row and panel 2.
decisions.correction: Marthanda Varma must match his V13 varma-v1 sheet and the page's earlier panels: the same narrow face with the curled moustache, the red-and-white Vaishnavite forehead mark, pearl drop earrings (no gold stud), and jet-black hair with NO grey anywhere, worn bare-headed in his field look as a side knot above his LEFT ear, never a topknot on the crown, so he can never be mistaken for Nagoji's later topknot look; bare-chested, cream mundu with a gold border, gold necklaces, the folded blue cloth over his arm. As he walks in from the right, his head is turned toward the distant sea behind him where the Dutch hulls ride at anchor, his eyes on the ships, not on the officers. Nagoji keeps his arms folded but both tunic sleeves are down to the wrists, so neither forearm shows any scar or mark; his right forearm is never scarred. Keep everything else that worked: Lannoy at left in the white tunic-coat, white mundu and sandals, and Nagoji in rust-red turban, red sash, boots and talwar, both watching Varma approach; the drill ground with the white-clad musket line, coconut palms, plain unlettered blue flags, the low wall and the anchored ships on the sea; and the open sky across the top centre left clear for the lettering.

decisions.issues: Acceptable, and the panel has no lettering. Lannoy, still in his white coat and mundu, lifts a short blue coat with brass buttons from a growing pile of coats and stiff felt tricornes. The men around him look sour. Nagoji has his arms folded and is on model: rust-red turban, clean chin, gold stud, no grey. Minor: the surrounding men already wear blue sleeveless waistcoats, and the background ranks wear blue vests and caps, which slightly blunts the 'only the pile is blue' beat. Nagoji's folded forearms show no brand; acceptable, since the inner forearms are turned in. No text. Hands are sound.

Strong staging: Nagoji whispers behind his cupped hand to Lannoy, he is on model, and there is clear sky at top right. It fails the ch16 bible row on the arms. Nagoji's RIGHT forearm (the near arm, hanging at his side) has two long white scars in the foreground, and the left-forearm brand sits near the elbow instead of a hand's width above the wrist. This contradicts panel 2 on the same page, where the brand and scar are correctly on the left forearm only. Also: grey at the temple follows the ch16 bible row but not the script's 'no grey yet'; the author needs to decide that one.
decisions.correction: Nagoji's RIGHT forearm, the arm hanging at his side nearest the viewer, is smooth unmarked skin with no scars: roll that sleeve down to the wrist. The brand and scar appear ONLY on his LEFT forearm, the arm raised to cup his mouth: on its inner side, a hand's width above the wrist, a single pale puckered patch of raised ridges blurred past reading (no letters, not a cross), with ONE long, thin, straight white scar running from the wrist toward the elbow beside it, and nothing near the elbow. Keep everything else exactly as it is: Nagoji leaning in to speak low into Lannoy's ear behind his cupped hand, his rust-red turban, red sash, talwar, thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin and small gold ear stud; Lannoy in the white tunic-coat with his hands behind his back, looking sidelong at him; the drill ground with the musket line, palms, the viewing stand and the sea; and the open sky at the top right left clear for the lettering.

decisions.issues: Clean. Lannoy matches his sheet: pale curly hair tied with a black ribbon, white tunic-coat, mundu and sandals, and he gestures at the infantry. The infantry are bare-chested in hitched dhotis with muskets on their shoulders. Nagoji has his arms crossed, unconvinced, in the rust-red turban, cream tunic, red sash, boots and talwar, with a clean chin, a small gold stud and no grey. The conch banner carries no text, and the ship is only a tiny hull on the horizon. There is a large clear sky at upper right for both Lannoy balloons and the caption.

Acceptable with minor notes. Nagoji rides at the head and flank of the line rather than strictly behind it. The stiff plumed caps read slightly like later shakos, but the script asks for stiff hats and panel 14.3 matches them. Varma on the dais is a little larger than 'small in the distance'. Otherwise the panel is on beat: Nagoji on a grey horse with a black mane (Megha), blue drill coat with the collar tight, rust-red turban on, clean chin, gold stud and no grey. Varma wears the cream-and-gold turban with the peacock crest, which is correct for the dais. The infantry wear blue coats over dhotis and are barefoot, with their muskets at one angle. There are drummers and a conch-on-red banner with no text, and the ship is only a tiny hull on the horizon. The upper-right sky is clear for the long caption.

In v01, Nagoji has a clear grey streak at the temple, but the script and MUST MATCH say no grey through 14.3. The infantry's hats are black tricornes. That doesn't match the tall stiff plumed hats of the same men in 14.2, and tricornes read as European or VOC troops. Two grinning soldiers at right have long curly black hair, curled moustaches, gold ear studs and grey at the temple, so they read as doubles of Nagoji. With his sleeves rolled and his hand on the hilt, the brand shows on the outer (back) surface of his left forearm instead of the inner forearm. The fall-out beat itself works: open coats, loosened dhotis, men grinning, Nagoji standing apart in his foreign cloth, with open sky above.
decisions.correction: Nagoji's hair is entirely jet black at the temples and behind the ears, with no grey or silver strands. Ignore 'first grey at the temples' in the LOOKS line for this panel. He wears the same blue Travancore drill coat as in the parade panel, now unbuttoned, with the sleeves down to the wrists so no brand or scar shows. The infantry's hats are the same tall, stiff, flat-topped dark blue hats with a white plume and a small brass badge from the parade panel, pushed back on their heads or held in their hands. No tricornes and no brimmed European hats anywhere. None of the soldiers wears an ear stud or has grey-streaked hair. Give them varied looks: short hair, Nair forelocks or small topknots, some clean-shaven, some with plain moustaches, so none can be mistaken for Nagoji. Keep everything else as it is: Nagoji standing at left, hands on hips, sceptical, the men in their blue coats shrugged open over bare chests and loosened white dhotis, sitting and standing, grinning up at him, the drill ground, wall and palms, and the open sky across the top left clear for the caption.

decisions.issues: Acceptable. Revathi matches her sheet: indigo sari with gold, jasmine braid, flat-coin necklace, armlets, sandalwood line, and no tali. Nagoji matches the commander look and the bible: rust-red turban, red sash, thick curled moustache, clean chin, small gold stud, and faint first grey at the temples, as the script asks from 14.4. The Velinadu muster is right: bare-chested men in white mundus with no coats, firing in turn from standing and kneeling ranks, under the red banner with the silver conch. Revathi looks toward the formations, not at him. Minor points: the two stand close side by side rather than at an obviously formal distance. The brand shows on the top of his crossed forearm. The conch has some faint interior shading but no lettering. Lettering space on the left is tight. Put Revathi's balloon in the sky above her head (top left). Put Nagoji's balloon in the sky between his turban and the flag. The caption fits in the open sky at upper right or as a slim box along the top-left edge. None of these needs to cover a face.

Clean. Revathi is close and matches her sheet: indigo sari with gold zari, a jasmine braid, the flat-coin necklace, gold armlets and the sandalwood line at the hairline. She has no tali and no red dot. The warm tone in her hair parting matches her approved sheet and does not read as sindoor. Gun smoke drifts behind her. Bare-chested infantry in white mundus fire under the conch-on-red banner on the red earth, with the Kovilakam roofs in the distance, which is consistent with panel 14.4. A small second pale line sits mid-forehead, which is minor. The upper-right sky is clear for both balloons.

Accepted with minor notes. The beat reads well: a line of young recruits in white sleeveless tunics and white mundus, crossed leather belts, blue waistbands and white turbans, barefoot, bringing flintlocks to the shoulder. This matches the bible's Travancore regulars. The flag on the right is a large plain white flag, not the Travancore standard (silver conch on red), and could read as a surrender flag. A tiny figure on the pavilion wears a rust-red turban and may have a dark chin, so it could be mistaken for Nagoji. There is no text, gore or anachronism, and the hands hold up at this scale. Wide open sky across the top middle has room for both captions.

This one is acceptable and fixes everything wrong with r1. Nagoji matches his sheet: thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, tiny flush gold stud, grey at the temples, an unreadable guarded face, and commander dress (rust-red turban, cream tunic with sleeves rolled, broad red sash, boots, talwar). The recruits continue panel 15.1: barefoot, white tunics and mundus, blue waistbands, crossed belts, flintlocks raised in one line on sand. Background officers wear white turbans and pale coats. There are no flags, no smoke and no clone of Nagoji's look. The upper-right sky is clear for the caption. Minor flaws: (1) The starburst brand sits correctly on his lower (LEFT) crossed forearm, but a thin pale scar streak runs ACROSS the upper (RIGHT) forearm. The bible puts that scar along the left forearm, wrist to elbow. It is small at page size; a retouch could remove it. (2) Tiny engraving squiggles on the musket lock plates cannot be read at print size. (3) The temple grey is a little stronger than 'faint', but it matches the picks for 15.4 and 15.6.

Accepted with minor notes. The memory is in dry Deccan colours: black soil, a man in a white pagdi and angarkha walking the field with a hoe, mesas and tiled village houses. In the doorway are the father (white-haired, bent, white pheta, black wool kambal, coarse dhoti, staff) and the mother (white hair, green glass bangles, turmeric-yellow hands). The mother's sari falls as a straight skirt and is not clearly the bible's kashta drape. The field man has a short beard rather than Bhalerao's thin young moustache, but his face is turned away and tiny. There is no text and the hands hold up. The open sky at upper left has room for both captions, even at inset size.

Accepted with minor notes. Nagoji matches his sheet: rust-red turban, cream tunic, red sash, thick curled moustache, clean chin, gold stud, grey at the temples. Dhanaji matches his: white pagdi, indigo quilted tunic, short black beard, small gold hoop, talwar. They lean on a low laterite wall at night above a lamplit drill ground, and all four hands rest soundly on the stone. The small background musketeers wear blue coats with baggy white trousers and dark footwear, where the script asks for dhotis and bare feet. They also differ from the white-clad 15.1 recruits, though it is a different, night company. The wooden structure behind them is a watch platform with no rope or noose. The lamps are open flames, not glass. The starry sky at upper right is clear for both balloons.

This one is acceptable and fixes everything wrong with r1. It is a closer chest-up two-shot of both men leaning on the same laterite wall as 15.4, at night, with blue-coated musketeers loading by open-flame lamps below. Dhanaji is on the left, as in 15.6: white pagdi, indigo quilted tunic, short black beard, small gold hoop, stockier build, squinting sideways at Nagoji. Nagoji wears commander dress with no blue coat: rust-red turban, cream tunic with sleeves rolled, red sash, talwar hilt. He has the thick curled moustache, clean chin, tiny gold stud and grey at the temple. All four hands rest soundly on the stone. There is no text, and the ship is only a tiny shape on the horizon. Minor flaws: (1) Nagoji's hooded eyes look level and to the left, past Dhanaji, rather than clearly down at the lamps. The guarded beat still reads. (2) Light stubble shading shows on his jaw, but the chin reads clean-shaven against Dhanaji's beard. (3) The space for balloons is the dark sky band at the top and the gap between the two turbans (about x 0.33 to 0.60, y 0 to 0.25). The three balloons will fit there but are tight and may overlap the tops of the turbans, never a face.

Accepted with minor notes. Dhanaji laughs and waves a hand, with drawn head-shake motion arcs (not text). He matches his sheet: white pagdi, indigo quilted tunic, short black beard, gold hoop. Nagoji, with the corner of his mouth lifting, matches his: rust-red turban, cream tunic, red sash, clean chin, gold stud, grey at the temples. The hands hold up. The pair read as being at ground level on the drill ground rather than at the low wall of 15.4, a small continuity drift. The background infantry wear blue coats with trousers and boots rather than dhotis and bare feet. One tiny bearded figure on the pavilion at far right wears a reddish turban. The dark sky between and around the two heads is clear for both balloons.

Minor: Nagoji's ear ornament is drawn as a tiny two-bead drop instead of the flush gold stud from the 2026-10-02 author decision. It is only about 11 px tall in this wide shot, so a quick retouch to a flush stud is advised. Otherwise it is clean: dusk bastion over the inlet with boats below; Nagoji has the rust turban, sash, cream tunic and trousers, boots, talwar, a clean chin and a faint white scar on the outer left forearm; Lannoy is bare-headed with pale hair, white tunic-coat, mundu and sandals; hands are sound; there is no text. The figures are lit rather than in true silhouette, but both read clearly. A large pewter-and-orange sky across the top half gives room for all three lines.

Minor only. Nagoji's head-shake is shown as a sceptical sidelong look with folded arms rather than a literal shake, which still reads as the beat. The grey at his right temple is a little stronger than 'faint' but stays at the temple. Otherwise clean: his chin is clean-shaven, the gold ear stud is small and flush, and the brand stays hidden. Lannoy matches his sheet (pale hair with a black ribbon, white tunic-coat over a mundu) and turns to Nagoji with a thin smile. The bastion, parapet, cannon, inlet with Marakkar boats and dusk light match 16.1 and 16.2. No painted text, and the hands are sound. The open dusk sky in the upper left and top centre leaves room for Lannoy's three speeches.

Minor only. Nagoji's grey at the temple is slightly stronger than 'faint'. A small domed sentry turret on the far left was not in 16.1 or 16.2 but fits the fort. Otherwise clean: Nagoji leans with his forearms on the parapet, with a clean chin, curled moustache, flush gold stud, rust-red turban, red sash and boots. Lannoy stands beside him in profile, eyes on the water, in his white coat, mundu and sandals with his hands behind his back. The room, light and costumes match the neighbouring panels. No painted text, and the anatomy is sound. Open sky across the top centre and upper right leaves room for both balloons.

Clean. Lannoy matches his sheet (pale hair with a black ribbon, white tunic-coat and mundu) and is turning a stone chip at dusk on the parapet. Nagoji is cropped at the left edge as the script asks, with a curled moustache, clean chin (only faint shading), gold stud and grey temples. The open sky at upper right takes both balloons.

Minor only. The faint grey at Nagoji's temples does not show under the turban. His ear stud is a small round bead, but it sits on the lobe with nothing hanging from it. The sunset is warmer than 'old pewter', but it matches the orange dusk of 17.1 and 17.4. Otherwise clean: Lannoy (pale hair with black ribbon, white tunic-coat, mundu, sandals) has his arm still extended after the throw and the stone arcs over the water. Nagoji stands to the left, as in 17.1, in rust-red turban, cream tunic, red sash, boots and talwar, with a thick moustache and a clean chin, watching the stone. The cannon embrasure is on the laterite parapet. Hands are sound and there is no text. Open sky at the upper middle and upper right leaves room for both balloons.

Minor only. The square glass ink bottle looks slightly modern. The rendering is more painterly than inked. Otherwise clean: a pale-haired boy of about ten works at a wooden desk in a whitewashed schoolroom with leaded windows and cold grey light. He draws a star-shaped fortress with compasses and a ruler. The plan is only lines and angles, with no people and no writing or numerals, and the ruler carries no markings. The only figure is the boy, and the grown De Lannoy is absent. Hands are sound. The plain grey wall between the window and the crucifix, and above the coat rack, leaves clear room for both off-panel balloons.

Acceptable, with minor notes. Lannoy has turned to Nagoji with an open palm toward the parapet and fort, and the last light falls between them. Nagoji matches his sheet (clean chin, grey temples, gold stud) and stands with his arms crossed. On his LEFT forearm, the brand sits mid-forearm toward the elbow on the visible outer side, not a hand's width above the wrist on the inner side, and the white scar runs diagonally across the forearm instead of lengthwise. Both are small at panel scale, and the brand is a blurred patch, not a cross or letters. The sun sits just above the horizon, slightly earlier than in 17.2. Three balloons fit in the sky above and between the heads.

Clean. A dim Flemish Gothic church: an elderly grey-haired woman in a dark fringed shawl lights a candle with a taper at a side altar, before an iron rack of votive flames, with a Madonna statue above. There is no text, the hand is sound, and nothing is anachronistic. The dark upper-left vault and window wall hold both off-panel lines without covering her face or the candles.

Minor only: at close zoom Nagoji's gold ear ornament has a tiny bead under the lobe stud, so it reads almost like a small drop, though at reading size it is a small gold stud. The grey at his temple is a little stronger than 'faint'. His crossed arms hide the inner-left-forearm brand and scar, which is acceptable because they are not called for in this beat. Otherwise it is clean. Lannoy matches his sheet (pale curly hair with black ribbon, white tunic-coat, mundu, sandals) and turns from the water toward Nagoji with a hand on the parapet. Nagoji (rust turban, curled moustache, smooth chin, cream tunic, red sash, boots) faces him squarely. The setting is a laterite bastion with a cannon embrasure in the last light, with small sailing boats on the inlet. There is no text, and the hands are sound. Both lower corners are open floor for the 18.2 inset, and the sky between and to the right of the heads is wide and clear for four lettering areas.

Minor: where the rope fails, near the hull, the frayed strands bunch into a lump that could, looked at closely, be read as a small knot. At inset size it reads as the wet, fraying break the script asks for. The line is otherwise straight and taut and runs out of frame at top right, with no loop or noose. The hand is anatomically sound and slips from the line in a torn grey-brown sleeve (Keshavrao's colour). There is no face, no figure, no blood and no text, and the cold storm palette is right.

Minor only. The background Nair guards carry spears and wear their topknots on the crown rather than tied forward. Nagoji's ear ornament is a small gold bead rather than a perfectly flush stud, the same as in the accepted page 16 and 17 frames. Everything the beat needs is present: Udayagiri's granite hill, the new angled bastions, the wall walk, the ditch, and scrub with one small muzzle flash and puff of smoke at right. Lannoy (white coat and mundu, sandals) points along the wall and Nagoji (rust-red turban, commander dress, clean chin, faint grey) walks beside him. The large dusk sky at upper right leaves clear room for both captions. No text, and the hands are sound. The frame is 1536 px wide; as the script notes, it needs a 2x upscale to reach 300 PPI at full width.

Framing is a chest-up close shot rather than truly tight on the ear. The lifting strand is a few loose locks trailing off the far side of his head, where his hidden right ear is, which is subtle but readable with 18.3 and 18.5 on either side. His sidelong, half-startled look fits 'not yet understood'. Lannoy matches his sheet (pale wavy hair with black ribbon, long nose, white stand-collar tunic-coat). The background guards are bare-chested here but wear sleeveless white tunics in 18.3, a small inconsistency in incidental figures. No text, no gore.

Minor. The spray of stone chips bursts from the parapet top level with Nagoji's shoulder, not near his knee as scripted; it still clearly shows a shot striking the parapet beside him. A plain white pennant flies on the wall at upper left. It has no text but could faintly suggest a flag of truce, and it does not appear in 18.3. Otherwise sound. Nagoji (rust-red turban, clean chin, curled moustache, gold stud, faint grey) drags Lannoy (white coat, mundu, sandals) down behind the parapet. The hands are anatomically correct, and the outer left forearm correctly shows no brand. The sky above and right of the turban gives room for the short 'Down!' balloon without covering a face.

Clean. Sentries snatching muskets, dogs barking, torches running for the ditch, empty scrub beyond, night falling. The alarm is blown on a horn rather than a whistle, which reads the same. No text, blood or anachronism. The open sky at upper right is clear for the caption.

Clean. An open palm (anatomy sound, thumb plus four fingers) holds three torn paper cartridge twists with black powder grains, with no casings or brass. It is torchlit by the bank below the wall, and the open dark sky at top left takes the caption. Minor: the grass is not obviously trampled, and the sentries wear white turbans with red bands rather than a distinctly Nair look; the current 19.1 does not match this, and the 19.1 correction asks it to.

Otherwise strong. Ramayyan matches his sheet (receding hair, white cloth, palm leaves and stylus, seated by the lamp). Lannoy is in the white coat, mundu and sandals with his pale hair ribboned, apart, turning the chipped stone. Nagoji stands by the door with the rust-red turban, thick curled moustache, clean chin, gold ear stud, grey at the temples, red sash and talwar. There is good dark wall space for three balloons. The failure is Nagoji's bare, crossed forearms: on the LEFT forearm's visible outer face, a white scar runs ACROSS the arm through a horizontal mottled patch. Together they read as a cross-shaped mark. The bible says the scar runs along the forearm from wrist toward elbow, beside a brand on the INNER forearm that is 'not a cross'.
decisions.correction: Keep this exact composition, guardroom, lamplight and all three figures unchanged: Ramayyan seated with his palm-leaf bundles and stylus, Lannoy apart in his white coat and mundu turning the chipped parapet stone, Nagoji standing by the door with arms folded. Change only Nagoji's sleeves. His cream tunic sleeves come all the way down to his wrists and stay down, so no forearm skin shows and NO scar, brand, slash, cross or mark of any kind is visible on either arm. Keep his rust-red turban, grey at the temples, thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, small gold ear stud, broad red sash and talwar exactly as they are.

decisions.issues: Acceptable. The setting is a morning audience in an open pillared hall. Varma is bare-headed with a knot above and behind his left ear, no turban or crest, bare-chested, with gold necklaces and a cream-and-gold cloth, stern and gesturing as he speaks. Nagoji matches his sheet (rust-red turban, clean chin, gold stud, grey at the temples). His visible forearm is unmarked and his left arm is out of view. Lannoy is in the white coat, mundu and sandals. Two bare-chested guards in white mundus flank the frame with curved swords; the right one also has a round shield. Hands are sound. Minor: the guards' topknots are tied high on the crown rather than forward-tied. The left guard's shield is out of view. Varma's hair is curlier than on the V13 sheet, and he wears a gold stud rather than pearl drops. Varma's two balloons fit over the ceiling beams at top centre and right.

Nagoji (rust-red turban, clean chin, gold stud, grey at the temples, unmarked forearms) and Lannoy (white coat, mundu, sandals) are good, leaving the same hall as in 19.4, and the upper hall and courtyard have caption space. The two Nair guards are wrong. They carry SPEARS instead of the swords the script calls for. They also wear a white upper cloth over one shoulder, red waist sashes and sandals. In 19.4, where the script fixes their look for pages 19 to 21, they are bare-chested in plain white mundus with no sash and carry long curved swords, one with a round shield. Nagoji's talwar hilt also has a disc guard like a Japanese tsuba.
decisions.correction: Keep Nagoji, Lannoy, the pillared hall, the brass lamps, the morning courtyard light and the walking composition exactly as they are. Change only the two Nair guards walking a few paces behind, to match the guards established in panel 19.4. Each carries a long curved Nair sword held point-down in the right hand and a small round black shield with brass bosses on the left arm. There are NO spears, lances or poles anywhere in the panel. Both are bare-chested with NO upper or shoulder cloth, wear only a plain white mundu with no red sash or coloured border, and go barefoot with no sandals. Their hair is in a high Kerala topknot, they have moustaches and scarred forearms, and they wear no sacred thread or forehead marks. Nagoji's talwar keeps the Indian disc-pommel hilt from his sheet, with no tsuba-like guard.

decisions.issues: Minor only. Nagoji matches the sheet and the ch16 row: rust-red turban, red sash, curled moustache, clean chin, gold stud, first grey at the temples. The Nair shadow stands a few paces off with topknot, white cloth, sword and round shield, but wears a toga-like shoulder drape where 20.4 shows him bare-chested with a narrow shoulder cloth. The left-forearm brand is drawn as a small fern-like branching mark near the elbow, with no long white scar beside it. Panels 20.2 and 20.4 show a round puckered patch plus the scar. It is not letters or a cross and is tiny at print size; retouch it if convenient. There is a large clear dusk sky at upper right for both captions.

Minor only. Closer shot of Nagoji at the parapet, gazing right toward the dark hills, left hand resting on the stone. Face is on model with clean chin, curled moustache, stud and grey temples. The forearm shows the puckered patch and long white scar, matching 20.4. The tiny background Nair carries a spear and a cross-strap instead of the sword seen in 20.1 and 20.4; he is barely visible. Same dusk wall and lighting as 20.1 and 20.4. There is a large clear sky at upper right for the caption.

Clean. Revathi matches her sheet: indigo sari with gold zari, jasmine braid, gold armlets, the sheet's gold necklace, sandalwood line, and no tali, which is correct before ch20. She stands speaking openly in a pillared Kerala hall before seated listeners. The lamps are brass with open wicks, and there is no text. Plain plastered wall above and to the right of her head (about x 0.40 to 0.65, y 0.0 to 0.35) and at upper left holds the caption.

Minor only. Nagoji steps away from the parapet, his left hand just off the stone. His body turns from the hills while his head still glances back toward them, which reads as the turning moment. His face is on model. The left forearm shows the pale puckered brand and long white scar with no letters and no gore. Behind him the Nair shadow stands with weight shifted: topknot, bare chest, white mundu, sword in hand, round shield. Same dusk wall as 20.1 and 20.2. There is clear sky at upper right and above the walls at upper left for the two captions.

Minor: the two Nair shadows at far left carry spears with their round shields instead of the long Nair sword fixed at 19.4 and shown in 20.1 and 21.2. They are small and half cropped, so this is a small prop mismatch, not a reason to reject. Everything else matches: Lannoy fits his sheet (pale hair tied with a black ribbon, white tunic-coat over a white mundu, sandals). Nagoji has the rust-red turban, a thick curled moustache, a clean chin, a gold ear stud, first grey at the temples, sash, talwar and boots. The test cannon fires from the lower battery, with smoke over the water and birds bursting from the trees. Hands are sound and there is no text. The upper-right dusk sky (about x 0.45 to 1.0, y 0 to 0.27) is open space for all three balloons.

Minor only. At heavy zoom, a dark ink line along Nagoji's jaw could be read as a thin chin-strap beard. His head is only about 45 px tall, so at print size it reads as jaw shading, the same shading seen in 21.1 and on the sheet. His ear stud and temple grey are too small to see at this scale. The Nairs' topknots sit on the crown rather than tied forward. Everything else follows the r1 correction. It is a true wide shot in the last light, with all four figures small on the southern wall walk, looking out at the setting sun over the river. Nagoji has the rust-red turban, curled moustache, cream tunic, red sash, cream trousers, boots and talwar. Lannoy matches his sheet: pale curly hair tied with a black ribbon, a white tunic-coat over a white mundu, and sandals. The two Nair shadows stand a few paces behind them, bare-chested, with white mundus, long swords and round shields. There is no flag and no painted text, and the palette matches the bastions, palms and river of 21.1. The upper half of the frame (about y 0.02 to 0.38, full width) is open sunset sky with thin cloud, room for both captions and the separate weighted one.

Minor: the men wear plain white short-sleeved upper garments with a pale cloth at the waist above their dhotis, not specified but plausible, and not a blue or red coat. This version fixes both r1 failures. The top edge of the frame now does the crop, so there are no heads and no impossible parapet overlap: each figure stands whole in front of the wall. Five barefoot men in white dhotis march left to right in step. Each holds a flintlock upright at the shoulder, gripping the wrist of the stock, with the butt at the hip and the barrel rising out of the top of the frame. Hands, feet and the flintlock parts are sound, and there is no text. The dusk light, river, hills and fort walls match 21.1 and 21.2. The left 40 percent of the strip has no figures, only sky over a dark, plain parapet wall and flagstones. The long caption can sit upper left (about x 0.02 to 0.40, y 0.03 to 0.45), and the weighted caption lower left on the wall or flagstones (about x 0.02 to 0.35, y 0.55 to 0.9).
